title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let Π̂_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free profinite on two generators. Let ρ (order 3) and σ_∞ (order 2) be the automorphisms induced by the S_3-symmetries of the three points. M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of 'loop-preserving' (inertia-preserving) automorphisms u of Π̂_{0,3} (or of an extension Π^{~}). Its image in the outer automorphisms is N_{0,3}^{!~}. This is the setting of what is now called the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT, in its version with the S_3-symmetry built in.

Invariants of u (from the previous pages):
- f is the conjugating element, with u(σ_∞) = inn(f^{-1})(η σ_∞) and u(ρ) = inn(f^{-1})(ξ ρ).
- g and h measure the failure of u to commute with ρ and σ_∞: u ρ u^{-1} = int(g) ρ, and similarly for h with σ_∞.
- α_0, β_0 are 'square roots' of g, h: g = α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1}.
- α = f α_0 and β = f β_0, with α ρ(α)^{-1} = ξ and β σ_∞(β)^{-1} = η (equation 47).

Section 5 has two parts.

(i) Behaviour under inner automorphisms. Take u' = int(γ)∘u with γ ∈ Π̂_{0,3}. Then (49):
- f' = f γ^{-1};
- g' = γ g ρ(γ)^{-1} and h' = γ h σ_∞(γ)^{-1};
- α_0' = γ α_0 and β_0' = γ β_0;
- α' = α, β' = β, ξ' = ξ, η' = η.

These can be checked directly. For example, u' ρ u'^{-1} = int(γ) int(g) ρ int(γ)^{-1} = int(γ g ρ(γ)^{-1}) ρ. Also f' α_0' = f γ^{-1} γ α_0 = f α_0. Hence α and β depend only on the outer class of u, i.e. its image in N_{0,3}^{!~}.

Grothendieck draws a methodological conclusion. The previous page objected that ξ, η are weak data, e.g. after projecting to SL(2,Ẑ). He therefore prefers parametrizing u by (α, β, f) rather than (ξ, η, f). He also prefers it to (α_0, β_0, f) or (g, h, f), which are not invariant under inner automorphisms.

(ii) Set-up of the composition law. For u'' = u'u in M_{0,3}^{!~}, he lists the three families of invariants (51). The next page derives the cocycle relations:
- g'' = u'(g) g', h'' = u'(h) h', f'' = f' u'(f);
- α_0'' = u'(α_0) α_0';
- α'' = (f'u')(α) α'.

It also mentions an ambiguity f ↦ l_0^n f, to be killed by a gerbe extension of M by Ẑ.

Purpose. This is bookkeeping toward describing the loop-preserving automorphism group (a GT-like group) through cocycles.
errors: No error found. The formulas (49) are consistent with the conventions of the previous page: u'ρu'^{-1} = int(γgρ(γ)^{-1})ρ and fα_0 is invariant.

Minor ambiguity: ξ, η are also inner-invariant by (49). So the stated advantage of (α, β, f) over (ξ, η, f) is not inner-invariance, which they share. It is presumably the finer information discussed on the previous page. The inner-invariance advantage applies only against (α_0, β_0, f) and (g, h, f).

ideas.what: Transformation of the invariants of a loop-preserving automorphism of π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) under composition with an inner automorphism; α, β depend only on the outer class.
ideas.modern_name: Parametrization of GT-type elements; passage from Aut to Out (GT̂ as a subgroup of Out F̂_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991) for GT̂; Lochak–Schneps and others for S_3-symmetric variants
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower; these computations are unpublished (Longue Marche follow-up)

ideas.what: Cocycle relations for the invariants under composition u''=u'u (set up here, completed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian 1-cocycles / crossed homomorphisms on GT-like groups

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct computation of how the invariants change under inner automorphisms, plus notation for compositions. The interesting gerbe remark is on the next page, not this one.
transcription_corrections: The heading is likely 'Composition avec automorphismes intérieurs. Relations de cocycles, pour un composé u''=u'u'.
'(48) u' = int(γ)∘u' — the image confirms int(γ).
In (49), the crossed-out material after f' = fγ^{-1} is illegible; the transcription's guess '[g'=γg, h'=γh]' is plausible.
The sentence probably reads: 'l'utilisation des (α,β,f) au lieu des (ξ,η,f), de préférence à (α_0,β_0,f) au lieu des (g,h,f)'. The second 'au lieu des' replaces the transcribed 'ou des'.
'automorphisme ext. à lacets' = outer loop-preserving automorphism; the image class is in N_{0,3}^{!~}.
